headword: {祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}

definitions.explanation: A monastery near the ancient Indian city of Śrāvastī, donated to the Buddha, where he often stayed and preached. In Japan the name is known above all from the famous opening line of The Tale of the Heike.

examples.japanese: {祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧。
examples.english: The sound of the bell of Jetavana.

examples.japanese: {祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦インド→インド：28735_indo⟧にあった⟦{寺院|じいん}→寺院：00122_jiin⟧だ。
examples.english: Jetavana was a monastery in India.

examples.japanese: ⟦{平家物語|へいけものがたり}→平家物語：31060_heikemonogatari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{冒頭|ぼうとう}→冒頭：11725_boutou⟧「{祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{中学校|ちゅうがっこう}→中学校：01465_chuugakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{暗唱|あんしょう}→暗唱：14801_anshou⟧⟦させられた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We had to memorize the opening of The Tale of the Heike, 'The sound of the bell of Jetavana', in junior high school.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The Tale of the Heike (⟦{平家物語|へいけものがたり}→平家物語：31060_heikemonogatari⟧) opens: {祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧、⟦{諸行無常|しょぎょうむじょう}→諸行無常：14481_shogyoumujou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{響|ひび}き→響き：00098_hibiki⟧あり (the bell of Jetavana echoes the impermanence of all things). Japanese schoolchildren learn the passage by heart, so the name instantly calls up the theme of impermanence and the fall of the proud.

WATCH OUT:
The ⟦{祇園|ぎおん}→祇園：31046_gion⟧ district of Kyoto and its Gion Festival take their name from the same source, through a shrine whose deity was linked to Jetavana, but the monastery itself was in India.
